# The ISLA forward pass {#sec-architecture}

*Before this chapter:* @sec-isla (the seven ideas of ISLA, each drawn on the
airfoil) and @sec-landscape (attention as a kernel integral operator, slice
attention, the transformer block). This chapter adds no idea; it states each
one exactly.

**This chapter is the specification of ISLA: every stage of the forward
pass, with one symbol per quantity, its tensor shape, and the identifier
that computes it.** @sec-isla says *why* each part is there; this chapter
says *what* the class computes, and the other chapters and the code are held
to it. Read it with @fig-isla-pass open: every stage below is one box of
that figure, and every code listing is cut out of the class's source by
symbol name as the page renders, so a listing cannot drift from the code it
shows. The chapter ends with where the time and memory of a training step go
on a GPU (@sec-arch-cost) and with the constructor's arguments
(@sec-arch-switches).

```{python}
#| label: setup-arch-source
#| include: false
# Code listings are extracted from the class's source files by symbol name as the page renders, so they cannot drift
# from the code: a renamed function or a moved marker comment fails the render instead of printing stale code.
import ast, textwrap
import physicsnemo
ISLA_SRC = Path(physicsnemo.__file__).parent / "experimental" / "models" / "isla"

def _symbol(tree, qualname):
    body, node = tree.body, None
    for part in qualname.split("."):
        node = next(n for n in body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) and n.name == part)
        body = node.body
    return node

_HISTORY = re.compile(r"20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d|former|hidden 192|PERF-")
def _drop_history_comments(block):
    """Drop every contiguous run of comment lines in which one line dates a measurement or recalls an earlier form."""
    out, run = [], []
    for l in block + [""]:
        if l.strip().startswith("#"):
            run.append(l); continue
        if not any(_HISTORY.search(c) for c in run):
            out += run
        run = []
        out.append(l)
    return out[:-1]

def listing(filename, qualname, start=None, end=None, docstring=False):
    """Print the source of `qualname` in `filename` as a fenced block; with `start`/`end`, only the lines of the
    function between the first line containing `start` and the next line containing `end` (end=None: to the end)."""
    src = (ISLA_SRC / filename).read_text(); lines = src.splitlines(); tree = ast.parse(src)
    node = _symbol(tree, qualname); a, b = node.lineno, node.end_lineno
    first = node.body[0]
    if not docstring and isinstance(first, ast.Expr) and isinstance(getattr(first, "value", None), ast.Constant) and isinstance(first.value.value, str):
        lines = lines[:first.lineno - 1] + lines[first.end_lineno:]; b -= first.end_lineno - first.lineno + 1
    block = lines[a - 1:b]
    block = _drop_history_comments(block)
    where = f"{filename}: {qualname}"
    if start is not None:
        i = next(k for k, l in enumerate(block) if start in l)
        j = next(k for k, l in enumerate(block) if end in l and k > i) if end else len(block)
        block = block[i:j]; where += f", from the line containing `{start}`" + (f" to the one containing `{end}`" if end else " to the end")
    print(f"```python\n# {where}\n" + textwrap.dedent("\n".join(block)).rstrip() + "\n```")
```

## Notation {#sec-arch-notation}

**One symbol per quantity, one code name per symbol.** Indices $i, j$ run
over the $N$ boundary tokens, $s, t$ over the $M$ slices, $k$ over the $K$
global directions, $q$ over the $Q$ prediction points of an interior task,
and $\beta$ over the named boundary conditions, with $\beta(i)$ the
condition of token $i$. The code carries a leading batch axis of one on
every tensor; the table omits it.

| symbol | shape | code | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\beta$ | one name each | `boundary_schemas`, `model.boundary_names` | the boundary conditions by name, stored sorted; each is one boundary mesh at full resolution with the per-cell fields it alone declares |
| $x_i, n_i, w_i$ | $N{\times}3,\ N{\times}3,\ N$ | `cell_centroids`, `cell_normals`, `cell_measures` of the boundary meshes | boundary token positions, normals, and the measure weight each token stands for: the cell's measure $\lvert C_i \rvert$ (its `_effective_measure` when the mesh stores one, else its geometric measure) on a surface task, its Horvitz–Thompson measure $\lvert C_i \rvert / \varpi_i$ on an interior task |
| $\varpi_i$ | per cell | `pi` in `sample_boundary_cells` | the probability that the interior task's draw keeps cell $i$ (@sec-arch-boundary-draw) |
| $g_k$, $\sigma$ | $K{\times}3$, $S$ | `global_schema` (rank 1, rank 0) | the problem's global vector inputs and global scalar inputs, as named fields (external aerodynamics: $K = 1$, the far-field direction) |
| $v_i$, $A_i$ | $N{\times}3$, $N{\times}3{\times}3$ per field | `boundary_schemas[name]` (rank 1, rank 2) | per-cell tensor inputs of one condition (an inlet's prescribed velocity, a loaded face's traction); none on the DrivAerML and AirfRANS tasks |
| $V_i$, $T_i$ | $N{\times}n_v{\times}3$, $N{\times}n_t{\times}3{\times}3$ | `vecs`, `tens` | the shared vector and tensor channels, onto which each condition's own maps (`vector_map`, `tensor_map`) take its vectors and tensors |
| $\hat g_k$, $\hat n_i$ | $K{\times}3$, $N{\times}3$ | `g_unit`, `n_hat` | the same directions and normals at unit length |
| $L$ | scalar | `gauge` | the length unit: the measure-weighted RMS pairwise distance of the full-resolution boundary |
| $r_i$ | $N{\times}3$ | `r` | position in length units, $x_i / L$; enters only inside differences |
| $\ell_i$ | $N$ | `log_w` | $\log w_i$, the measure bias of every softmax over tokens |
| $\eta_i$ | $N{\times}(1 + K + n_\beta + S)$ | `seed` (`_condition_tokens`) | the seed: the scalars a token has before any layer runs, a constant 1 first ($n_\beta$ counts the invariants of condition $\beta$'s fields) |
| $h_i$ | $N{\times}D$ | `h` | the token state, width $D$ (`hidden`) |
| $\tilde h_i$ | $N{\times}D$ | `h_n` | $\mathrm{LN}(h_i)$, the normalized state the slice sublayer reads |
| $\lambda_{is}$, $\lambda'_{is}$ | $N{\times}M$ | `logits`, `logits + bias` | routing logits before and after the geometric refinement |
| $a_{is}$ | $N{\times}M$ | `a` | routing weights: a softmax over tokens $i$ for each slice $s$ |
| $z_s, m_s$ | $M{\times}3$ | `z_pos`, `m_s` | the anchor of slice $s$: its mean position and its mean normal direction |
| $\rho_{is}$, $\xi_{is}$ | $N{\times}M{\times}3$, $N{\times}M{\times}(5 + K + n_v + n_t)$ | `rel`, `geo` | the token-to-anchor separation, and the relational invariants formed from it ($n_v$ shared vector channels and $n_t$ shared tensor channels; both zero on the DrivAerML and AirfRANS tasks) |
| $\pi_{is}$ | $N{\times}M$ | `point_mix` | read-back weights: a softmax over slices $s$ for each token $i$ |
| $\bar\xi_i$, $\gamma_i$ | $N{\times}(5 + K)$, $N{\times}D/2$ | `pooled`, `geo_pool` | the invariants pooled over slices, and their projection |
| $Z_s$ | $M{\times}D$ | `z` | the slice state |
| $b_i$ | $N{\times}D$ | `back` | the slice states read back to token $i$ |
| $\hat u_i$ | $N{\times}3$ | `r_hat` | the head's radial direction, from the token's own soft anchor to the token |
| $c_i$ | $N{\times}n_c$ | `coeffs` | the head's invariant coefficients, $n_c$ of them over all outputs |
| $p_q$, $\delta_q$, $u_q$ | $Q{\times}3$, $Q$, $Q{\times}3$ | `exact_boundary_geometry` (`wall_distance`, `wall_direction`) | an interior prediction point's closest point on the full-resolution boundary surface, its signed distance to it and the direction from it (@sec-arch-interior-geometry) |
| $s_q$, $\hat\nu_q$ | $Q$, $Q{\times}3$ | `s`, `q_nhat` | the signed distance in length units, $\delta_q / L$, and the point's direction $\operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\, u_q$, which plays the normal's part |

: The symbols of the forward pass, with the shape of each tensor at batch one and the identifier that holds it in the
code. How to read this: a row names a quantity, not a step; the stage that computes it is given where it first appears
below, and the table does not list the learned weights. {#tbl-arch-notation}

$\mathrm{LN}$ is LayerNorm over the width; $\mathrm{MLP}$ is
Linear–GELU–Linear with a hidden width of $4D$ (`MLP_RATIO`); $W$ with a
subscript is a learned affine map. Definitions use $\equiv$.

## The pass in one picture {#sec-arch-picture}

**From the inputs to the last slice layer, the model computes only scalars
that are invariant under rotation, translation and uniform rescaling.
Vectors are rebuilt once, at the output.** @fig-isla-pass is the whole
surface model. The interior task of @sec-arch-modes draws its boundary
tokens from the cells, adds the prediction points as tokens, and changes
which tokens the head reads; it adds no stage to the slice layers or the
head.

```{mermaid}

    FR["stage 1, frame:<br/>L = RMS pairwise distance; r<sub>i</sub> = x<sub>i</sub> / L;<br/>unit n̂<sub>i</sub>, ĝ<sub>k</sub>; ℓ<sub>i</sub> = log w<sub>i</sub>"]:::fixed
    SEED["stage 2, seed, in a block layout over the conditions:<br/>η<sub>i</sub> = [1, n̂<sub>i</sub>·ĝ<sub>k</sub>, the invariants of condition β(i)'s fields, σ]"]:::fixed

    LAYER["stage 3, slice layer × 12 (opened up in the next figure):<br/>routing a<sub>is</sub> → anchors z<sub>s</sub>, m<sub>s</sub> → invariants ξ<sub>is</sub> → refined routing<br/>→ slice states Z<sub>s</sub> → read-back → h<sub>i</sub> (N×D)"]:::learned
    HF["stage 4, head frame: soft anchors from the final state;<br/>û<sub>i</sub> = direction from the token's anchor to the token (N×3)"]:::fixed
    HEAD["stage 5, linear head on LN(h<sub>i</sub>):<br/>invariant coefficients c<sub>i</sub> (N × n<sub>c</sub>)"]:::learned
    BASIS["equivariant basis at each token:<br/>ĝ<sub>k</sub>, n̂<sub>i</sub>, û<sub>i</sub> and their tangential complements<br/>(N × (2K+3) × 3)"]:::fixed
    OUT["outputs: each declared field, contracted from c<sub>i</sub> and the basis<br/>(N, N×3, N×3×3, ...)"]:::out

    IN --> FR --> SEED --> EMB --> LAYER --> HEAD --> OUT
    LAYER --> HF --> BASIS --> OUT
    FR -. "r<sub>i</sub>, n̂<sub>i</sub>, ĝ<sub>k</sub>, ℓ<sub>i</sub> to every layer" .-> LAYER
```

## Stage 1: the boundary by condition, and the frame {#sec-arch-frame}

**The boundary arrives as named conditions, each one mesh at full
resolution, and the frame the model builds from it has a length unit and no
origin.** A boundary-value problem prescribes different data on different
parts of its boundary: a velocity at an inlet, a pressure at an outlet,
nothing but the wall itself on a no-slip body. ISLA takes the boundary in
that form. `boundary_meshes` maps each condition's name to one mesh, a
polyline in two dimensions or a surface in three, and that mesh's
`cell_data` holds the fields its condition declares and no others
(@sec-isla-inputs). The constructor fixes the names (`boundary_schemas`) and
stores them sorted (`model.boundary_names`). A name is a non-empty string
without `"."`, and it may not be an attribute of the `nn.ModuleDict` that
holds the conditions' parameters (`"keys"`, `"update"`, `"training"`, ...).
A forward pass takes any non-empty subset of the declared names in any
order; the model walks them in sorted order, so the order of the mapping
changes nothing, bitwise. An unknown name raises a `ValueError` that lists
the declared ones, and a condition left out contributes what a condition
with zero cells contributes: no tokens.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-conditions
#| output: asis
import yaml
import standing as S
CONF = Path(physicsnemo.__file__).parent.parent / "examples" / "cfd" / "external_aerodynamics" / "unified_external_aero_recipe" / "conf" / "model"
rows_c = []
for p in sorted(CONF.glob("isla_*.yaml")):
    mb = S.recipe_model(p.stem)   # with the constants it leaves to its dataset file, as train.py fills them
    if not mb.get("boundary_schemas"):
        continue
    m_c = ISLA(output_schema={"y": {"rank": 0}}, boundary_schemas=mb["boundary_schemas"], global_schema=mb.get("global_schema"),
               reynolds=mb.get("reynolds"), interior=bool(mb.get("interior")), hidden=8, n_layers=1, n_slices=2, dim=int(mb.get("dim", 3)))
    for name, c in m_c.boundary_conditions.items():
        fields = ", ".join(f"`{f}` ({s.rank})" for f, s in m_c.boundary_schemas[name].items()) or "none"
        nv = 0 if c.vector_map is None else c.vector_map.shape[1]
        rows_c.append((p.stem, "interior" if m_c.interior else "surface", name, fields, c.seed.in_features, nv, m_c.n_boundary_vecs))
out = "| configuration | task | condition | its fields (rank) | input-layer columns | its vectors | shared vector channels |\n|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|\n"
last = None
for cfg, task, name, fields, ncol, nv, nshared in rows_c:
    head = (f"`{cfg}`", task) if cfg != last else ("", "")
    out += f"| {head[0]} | {head[1]} | `{name}` | {fields} | {ncol} | {nv} | {nshared if cfg != last else ''} |\n"
    last = cfg
print(out)
print(": The boundary conditions of the recipe's ISLA configurations, read from `conf/model/isla_*.yaml` and built into the "
      "class as the page renders, conditions in the stored (sorted) order. The input-layer columns are $1 + K + n_\\beta + S$ "
      "(the constant, the $K$ normal-direction cosines, the invariants of the condition's own fields, the $S$ global "
      "scalars); a condition's vectors are its rank-1 fields, and the shared channels number as many as the widest "
      "condition has. How to read this: a condition without fields still has its own input layer; the table does not "
      "show the labels by which the lug, Tensile2d and DeepJEB++ datasets mark their conditions inside one mesh, which a "
      "recipe transform splits into these meshes before the model sees them (@sec-isla-inputs).")
```

Every cell is a candidate token, read off its mesh as its centroid $x_i$,
its normal $n_i$ and its measure $\lvert C_i \rvert$ (the length of a
segment, the area of a triangle: the cell's `_effective_measure` when the
mesh stores one, else its geometric measure). Before any token is chosen,
the model computes every cell's seed scalars (stage 2) in its condition's
columns of one block layout over all declared conditions, so the cells of
every condition form one token set of fixed width (`_condition_tokens`). A
surface task predicts at the cells it is given, so every cell is a token,
with $w_i = \lvert C_i \rvert$. An interior task draws its $N$ tokens from
the cells inside the forward pass and gives each the measure it stands for
(@sec-arch-boundary-draw).

The frame is built from the tokens, together with the global inputs $g_k$
and $\sigma$. The model normalizes every direction it is given,
$\hat g_k \equiv g_k / \lvert g_k \rvert$ and $\hat n_i \equiv n_i /
\lvert n_i \rvert$, so the magnitude of a global vector never enters; a
magnitude that matters is a global scalar input. The one length unit is a
normalized two-point integral of the boundary, with $\tilde w_i \equiv w_i /
\sum_j w_j$:

$$
L \equiv \Big( \sum_{i,j} \tilde w_i\, \tilde w_j\, \lvert x_i - x_j \rvert^2 \Big)^{1/2}
      = \Big( 2 \sum_i \tilde w_i\, \lvert x_i - \bar x \rvert^2 \Big)^{1/2},
\qquad
r_i \equiv x_i / L,
\qquad
\ell_i \equiv \log w_i .
$$

The code evaluates the second form (`rms_pairwise_distance`, $O(N)$
through the variance identity) over every cell of the full-resolution
boundary, each cell with its centroid $x_i$, its measure and its own second
moment about its centroid,
$J_i \equiv \frac{1}{(n+1)(n+2)} \sum_k \lvert v_k - x_i \rvert^2$ for an
$n$-simplex with vertices $v_k$ (a segment's $\ell^2 / 12$,
`cell_second_moments`), added to $\lvert x_i - \bar x \rvert^2$ in the
second form. With $J_i$ the sum is the exact RMS distance between two points
of the piecewise-flat surface, so a subdivision of the cells leaves $L$
unchanged to roundoff. The weighted mean $\bar x$ is an
intermediate of this scalar only and is never used as a center. $L$ is
unchanged by a rigid motion, scales with the geometry, is unchanged by a
uniform rescale of the weights (they are normalized first), and converges
under refinement of any boundary whose normalized measure converges
(@sec-isla-frame). The scaled positions $r_i$ never reach a learned map;
they enter only as the differences $r_i - z_s$ of stage 3 and $r_i - z^f$ of
stage 4. The log measure $\ell_i$ is the bias that makes every softmax over
tokens a quadrature rule (@sec-isla-quadrature). A boundary mesh without a
stored `_effective_measure` contributes its cells' geometric measures, so
$\ell_i$ is always defined. $L$ is computed in `forward` from the given
meshes before the interior task draws its tokens (`ISLA._gauge`), so on both
tasks it is the same for every draw of the boundary tokens. A model with
declared scales computes the case's velocity, density and Reynolds number at
the same point, in float64 (`ISLA._case_scales`), divides the declared inputs
by them before stage 2, and multiplies the outputs by them after stage 5
(@sec-using-scales).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Stage 1 in the code"}
Each condition's cells become rows of one token set in `forward`; the length unit is one function of the full-resolution cells, and the frame is a few lines of `_forward_tokens` (the token state then stores `r = points / gauge`): no center survives either.

### The interior task's boundary draw {#sec-arch-boundary-draw}

**The interior task draws its boundary tokens inside the forward pass: a
fixed budget of the full-resolution cells, shared over the conditions, each
cell kept with a probability proportional to its measure and carrying the
measure it stands for.** An interior task predicts at the prediction
points, so its boundary tokens are a quadrature of the surface, and the
model draws that quadrature itself (`sample_boundary_cells`). A surface task
predicts at every cell it is given and samples none; it accepts only the
default `boundary_tokens`.

The draw has three steps. The budget $B$ (`boundary_tokens`) is shared over
the given conditions by water filling: equal shares, a condition with fewer
cells than its share kept whole and its unused share given equally to the
others, until no share changes. Within a condition, each cell is kept with
a probability proportional to its measure, capped at one, the constant
chosen so that the probabilities add up to the condition's share. The cells
are then laid end to end along a line, the conditions in sorted order and
each condition's cells in the Morton (Z-order, a space-filling curve) order
of their centroids, each cell an interval as long as its probability, and
the cells under the points $u, u + 1, u + 2, \dots$ are kept: *systematic
sampling*, a single random start $u$ for the whole case. The Morton order is
taken along the dataset's axes, so once a boundary is subsampled a rotated
case draws other cells; @sec-isla-contracts states what that does to the pose
contract. @fig-arch-boundary-draw
runs the class's own draw on the airfoil.

```{python}
#| label: fig-arch-boundary-draw
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The interior task's boundary draw, run by the class's `sample_boundary_cells` on the airfoil at 160 cells, finer
#|   around the leading edge, with a budget of 32 tokens and the evaluation start $u = 1/2$. Top: each cell colored by
#|   its inclusion probability $\varpi_i$, proportional to its length; the kept cells' centroids as black dots. Bottom:
#|   the line of the systematic draw, the cells as intervals of length $\varpi_i$ in the Morton order of their centroids
#|   (the first eight units of the line); the draw keeps the cells under the points $u + m$ (the ticks), the blue
#|   intervals. How to read this: short cells are kept less often, and every kept cell stands for the same length, its
#|   own over $\varpi_i$, so the dots are spread by arclength, not by cell count; a training step draws a new $u$, so the
#|   dots move from step to step. It does not show the water filling over several conditions (the airfoil is one).
#| fig-height: 5.0
#| code-fold: true
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.sampling import sample_boundary_cells, pps_inclusion_probabilities
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.model import EVAL_START
from physicsnemo.mesh.spatial.bvh import _compute_morton_codes
frac_d = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(1.0 - 0.75 * np.sin(np.linspace(0, np.pi, 160)) ** 6)]); frac_d /= frac_d[-1]
JD = joukowski(n_cells=160, frac=frac_d)
a_d, x_d = torch.tensor(JD["w"]), torch.tensor(JD["mid"])
BUDGET_D = 32
pi_d = pps_inclusion_probabilities(a_d.double(), torch.tensor(float(BUDGET_D), dtype=torch.float64)).numpy()
kept_d, w_d = sample_boundary_cells([a_d], [x_d], BUDGET_D, torch.tensor(EVAL_START, dtype=torch.float64))
kept_d = kept_d.numpy()
order_d = _compute_morton_codes(x_d, isotropic=True).argsort(stable=True).numpy()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 5.0), gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[2.3, 0.8], hspace=0.35))
ax = axes[0]
norm_d = plt.Normalize(0, pi_d.max())
for i in range(len(a_d)):
    ax.plot(JD["xy"][i:i + 2, 0], JD["xy"][i:i + 2, 1], color=plt.cm.viridis(norm_d(pi_d[i])), lw=3.2, solid_capstyle="butt")
ax.plot(JD["mid"][kept_d, 0], JD["mid"][kept_d, 1], "o", color=INK, ms=4)
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")
sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm_d, cmap="viridis")
cb = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.01); cb.outline.set_visible(False)
cb.set_label(r"inclusion probability $\varpi_i$ [–]", fontsize=8.5); cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
ax = axes[1]
line_d = np.cumsum(pi_d[order_d]); start_d = line_d - pi_d[order_d]
kept_set = set(kept_d.tolist())
for j, c in enumerate(order_d):
    if start_d[j] > 8:
        break
    col = BLUE if c in kept_set else ("#d9d7cf" if j % 2 else "#bdbab0")
    ax.barh(0, min(pi_d[c], 8 - start_d[j]), left=start_d[j], height=0.6, color=col, edgecolor=WHITE, lw=0.4)
for m in range(8):
    ax.plot([EVAL_START + m] * 2, [-0.5, 0.5], color=INK, lw=1.0)
ax.set_xlim(0, 8); ax.set_ylim(-0.6, 0.6); ax.set_yticks([])
ax.set_xlabel(r"position along the line, cumulative $\varpi$ in the Morton order [–]")
for sp in ("top", "right", "left"): ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
plt.show()
```

In symbols, with $N_\beta$ the cell count of condition $\beta$, $B$ the
budget, $\lambda$ the water level (`water_fill`), $c_\beta$ the
proportionality constant of condition $\beta$
(`pps_inclusion_probabilities`) and $u$ the start:

$$
b_\beta = \min(N_\beta, \lambda), \quad \sum_\beta b_\beta = \min\Big(\sum_\beta N_\beta,\ B\Big);
\qquad
\varpi_i = \min\big(1,\ c_\beta \lvert C_i \rvert\big), \quad \sum_{i \in \beta} \varpi_i = b_\beta;
\qquad
w_i = \frac{\lvert C_i \rvert}{\varpi_i} .
$$

The draw keeps exactly $k = \min(\sum_\beta N_\beta, B)$ cells, a number
fixed by the cell counts alone, so the shapes are static and the draw
traces into one compiled graph. Over a uniform start each cell is kept with
probability exactly $\varpi_i$, and a cell with $\varpi_i = 1$ exactly
once. Each kept cell carries its Horvitz–Thompson measure $w_i$, the
importance weight of the survey-sampling literature, so for any per-cell
quantity $f$

$$
\mathbb{E}_u \Big[ \sum_{i \text{ kept}} w_i\, f_i \Big] = \sum_{\text{all cells}} \lvert C_i \rvert\, f_i ,
$$

and the sum is exact on a condition kept whole. Every measure-weighted
sum over the tokens (the slice states, the anchors, the prediction points'
routing mass) is therefore a quadrature of the full surface; the length unit
and the declared scales are computed from the full surface itself, before
the draw. The kept cells are spaced evenly in cumulative probability along
the space-filling curve, so the sample is spread over the surface rather
than clumped. In training $u$ is drawn uniform on $[0, 1)$ from the global
torch random-number generator at every step (`torch.manual_seed` reproduces
a run), so the model sees a new quadrature of the same surface each time;
in evaluation (`model.eval()`) $u = 1/2$ (`EVAL_START`), so inference is
deterministic. The selection runs without gradient, in float64 and outside
autocast, and the kept cells' measures keep their gradient. It selects rows
of the token set whose seeds stage 2 has already computed for every cell,
and returns them in the cells' own order, so a condition kept whole is its
mesh as given.

::: {.column-margin}
Why proportional to measure: an uncapped kept cell then stands for
$\lvert C_i \rvert / (c_\beta \lvert C_i \rvert) = 1 / c_\beta$, the same
measure for every token of its condition. The draw spends tokens where the
surface is, not where the mesher put its cells.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The boundary draw in the code"}
The water filling, the capped inclusion probabilities found exactly from the sorted measures, the systematic draw, and the lines of `forward` that pick the start and apply the draw.

## Stage 2: the seed and the embedding {#sec-arch-seed}

**A token's seed is a constant and every origin-free scalar its inputs
offer; its condition's own input layer maps the seed to the token width, and
the condition is known to the network by those parameters alone.** With no
origin, a position alone has no invariant. The only scalars of $\{\hat n_i,
\hat g_k\}$ that survive a rotation are the cosines between them. To them
the seed adds the invariants of the fields the token's condition declares
and the global scalar inputs, behind a constant 1. Each condition has its
own input layer (`boundary_conditions[name].seed`, a linear map without a
bias), so its column on the constant is the condition's learned offset: two
conditions that declare no field at all, a no-slip wall and a slip wall,
start from different states. A GELU and a linear layer shared by every
condition follow (`embed`). No input is a tag naming the condition (no
one-hot field): the condition's identity is in the parameters its tokens
read.

The tokens of all conditions are encoded in one matrix product. Each
token's seed sits in its condition's columns of a row as wide as all the
conditions' seeds together, with zeros in the other conditions' columns, and
the row multiplies the conditions' input layers placed side by side. That
is exactly each condition's own map, with shapes fixed whatever the draw
kept, and every condition's parameters take part in every pass, present or
not, which distributed training needs (a parameter that receives no gradient
stops it). @fig-arch-block-layout draws the layout for the AeroZoo
configuration's four conditions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-arch-block-layout
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The block layout of the seed, for the four conditions of the recipe's AeroZoo configuration
#|   (`isla_volume_aerozoo.yaml`), with the column widths read from the class (`ISLA._seed_columns`) as the page
#|   renders and six tokens per condition for the picture. Each row is one boundary token; its seed fills its own
#|   condition's columns (blue) and leaves zeros elsewhere (white), and one product with the four input layers side
#|   by side gives every token its own condition's map. How to read this: the column count of a block is that condition's
#|   $1 + K + n_\beta + S$ of @tbl-arch-conditions; in a real case the rows are the drawn tokens, mixed over the
#|   conditions in the draw's order, and their numbers follow the water filling, not six each.
#| fig-height: 3.0
#| code-fold: true
mb_az = S.recipe_model("isla_volume_aerozoo")
M_AZ = ISLA(output_schema={"y": {"rank": 0}}, boundary_schemas=mb_az["boundary_schemas"], global_schema=mb_az["global_schema"],
            reynolds=mb_az["reynolds"], interior=True, hidden=8, n_layers=1, n_slices=2)
cols_az, names_az, per = M_AZ._seed_columns, M_AZ.boundary_names, 6
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 3.0))
for b_, name in enumerate(names_az):
    y0 = (len(names_az) - 1 - b_) * per
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((0, y0), cols_az[-1], per, facecolor=WHITE, edgecolor=MUTED, lw=0.6))
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((cols_az[b_], y0), cols_az[b_ + 1] - cols_az[b_], per, facecolor="#e6f0fb", edgecolor=BLUE, lw=0.9))
    ax.text(-0.6, y0 + per / 2, f"tokens of {name}", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=INK)
    ax.text((cols_az[b_] + cols_az[b_ + 1]) / 2, len(names_az) * per + 0.6, f"{name}: {cols_az[b_ + 1] - cols_az[b_]} columns",
            ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8, color=INK)
for c in cols_az[1:-1]:
    ax.axvline(c, color=MUTED, lw=0.6)
ax.set_xlim(-0.2, cols_az[-1] + 0.2); ax.set_ylim(0, len(names_az) * per + 3)
ax.set_xlabel("seed column, all conditions side by side [–]"); ax.set_yticks([])
for sp in ("top", "right", "left"): ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
plt.show()
```

In symbols, with $W_\beta$ condition $\beta$'s input layer, $e_\beta$ its
column on the constant, and $W_e, b_e$ the shared linear layer,

$$
\eta_i \equiv \big[\, 1,\ \hat n_i \!\cdot\! \hat g_1,\ \dots,\ \hat n_i \!\cdot\! \hat g_K,\ \zeta_i,\ \sigma \,\big]
\quad (1 + K + n_\beta + S \text{ scalars}),
\qquad
h_i \equiv W_e\, \mathrm{GELU}\big(W_{\beta(i)}\, \eta_i\big) + b_e ,
$$

so $W_{\beta(i)} \eta_i = e_{\beta(i)} + {}$(the rest of the map on the
scalars). $\zeta_i$ are the invariants of the fields condition $\beta(i)$
declares and $\sigma$ the global scalar inputs, the same on every token. A
rank-0 field is its own scalar. A rank-1 field $v_i$ contributes $v_i \cdot
\hat n_i$, $v_i \cdot \hat g_k$, $\lvert v_i \rvert$ and its dot products
with the condition's other rank-1 fields. A rank-2 field $A_i$ contributes
$a^{\mathsf T} A_i b$ over the frame vectors $a, b \in \{\hat n_i, \hat
g_k\}$, its trace and its Frobenius norm (`_InputSet._features`). On the
DrivAerML Surface task there is one condition without fields, $K = 1$ and
$S = 0$, so the seed is two numbers per token, the constant and the cosine
between the normal and the far-field direction. With no global input and no
field ($K = n_\beta = S = 0$) the seed is the constant alone: every token of
a condition starts from the same learned state, and all separation between
its tokens comes from the slice layers.

**Vectors and tensors keep their rank.** A condition's rank-1 fields, and
the vectors $A_i \hat n_i$, $A_i \hat g_k$ (and $A_i^{\mathsf T} \hat n_i$,
$A_i^{\mathsf T} \hat g_k$ for a non-symmetric $A_i$) derived from its
rank-2 fields, are its $p_\beta$ vectors. Its own linear map
$\Phi_\beta$ (`vector_map`, $n_v \times p_\beta$) takes them onto $n_v$
shared vector channels, as many as the widest condition has, and its map
$\Psi_\beta$ (`tensor_map`) takes its rank-2 fields onto the shared tensor
channels:

$$
V_{ia} = \sum_{b} (\Phi_{\beta(i)})_{ab}\, v_{ib}, \qquad
T_{ia} = \sum_{b} (\Psi_{\beta(i)})_{ab}\, A_{ib} .
$$

A linear combination with scalar weights commutes with every orthogonal
map, $R \sum_b \Phi_{ab} v_b = \sum_b \Phi_{ab} R v_b$, so the channels
are true vectors and tensors like their inputs, and the slice layers
contract them with the token-to-anchor direction (stage 3, step d). Both
maps start as the identity padded with zeros, so condition $\beta$'s
$j$-th vector starts as channel $j$; a condition without vectors has no map
and carries zeros in the channels, as the prediction points do. The maps
run in the inputs' precision, outside autocast.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Stage 2 in the code"}
A condition's seed is the constant, the cosines against the global directions, its fields' invariants and the global scalars, in that order, placed in its block of the layout; `_InputSet._features` is where a rank-1 or rank-2 field becomes the invariants $\zeta_i$; `_boundary_channels` applies the conditions' input layers side by side, the shared layer, and the vector and tensor maps.

## Stage 3: the slice layer {#sec-arch-layer}

**A slice layer routes the tokens softly into $M$ slices, forms one anchor
per slice, describes every token relative to every anchor by invariant
scalars, and sends information up to the slices and back down together
with those scalars.** It is the one block that repeats, twelve times, each
copy with its own parameters (`_SliceBlock`), and every condition's tokens
route into the same slices, form the same anchors and read the same slice
states: that is how the conditions interact, and the cost does not grow with
their number. Its inputs are the token state
$h_i$ and the four frame quantities of stage 1, which every layer receives
unchanged: $r_i$, $\hat n_i$, $\hat g_k$, $\ell_i$. Its output is the updated
$h_i$.

Four pieces of transformer machinery appear in it (@sec-landscape). A
*softmax* over an index turns a vector of logits into nonnegative weights
that sum to one along that index. *LayerNorm* (LN) maps a token's state to
zero mean and unit variance across its $D$ channels, then applies a learned
per-channel scale and shift. The *residual stream* is the sequence of token
states $h_i$ that every sublayer updates additively, $h \leftarrow h +
f(h)$, so the network is a product of near-identity maps. A *pre-LN*
sublayer reads its input through a LayerNorm, $h \leftarrow h +
f(\mathrm{LN}(h))$, so the size of the stream never enters $f$. A slice
layer is two pre-LN sublayers: the slice sublayer (steps a to i) and the
token MLP (step j). @fig-isla-layer shows the ten steps, and the equations
follow in the same order.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-isla-layer
%%| fig-cap: >
%%|   One slice layer, opened up. Down the left: the routing path from the
%%|   normalized token state to the slice states. Down the right: the geometry
%%|   path from the routing weights to the anchors and the relational
%%|   invariants, which feed back into the routing (the refinement) and
%%|   forward into the read-back. Two softmaxes act on the same logits: over
%%|   tokens for the routing (each slice's weights sum to one, with the
%%|   measure bias) and over slices for the read-back (each token's weights
%%|   sum to one, without it). How to read this: every step of the slice
%%|   sublayer reads the normalized state $\mathrm{LN}(h_i)$, written $\tilde h_i$ in the text; the raw $h_i$
%%|   enters only the two residual additions and the LayerNorm of step j. Step e forms both the refined logits and the
%%|   read-back weights, and step h both the read-back and the pooled invariants. The only tensor that
%%|   is $N{\times}M$ in the width of the invariants is $\xi_{is}$, and it is
%%|   pooled to $N{\times}(5+K)$ before any learned projection
%%|   (@sec-arch-cost).
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 460}}}%%
flowchart TB
    classDef data fill:#f4f3ee,stroke:#898781,color:#0b0b0b
    classDef learned fill:#e6f0fb,stroke:#2a78d6,color:#0b0b0b
    classDef fixed fill:#ffffff,stroke:#2a78d6,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#0b0b0b

    H["token state h<sub>i</sub> (N×D);<br/>frame r<sub>i</sub>, n̂<sub>i</sub>, ĝ<sub>k</sub>, ℓ<sub>i</sub>"]:::data
    L1["a. normalized state LN(h<sub>i</sub>);<br/>routing logits λ<sub>is</sub> = τ cos(LN(h<sub>i</sub>), p<sub>s</sub>) (N×M)"]:::learned
    A0["b. provisional routing a⁰<sub>is</sub> =<br/>softmax over tokens of λ<sub>is</sub> + ℓ<sub>i</sub>"]:::fixed
    ANC["c. anchors z<sub>s</sub> = Σ<sub>i</sub> a⁰<sub>is</sub> r<sub>i</sub>,<br/>m<sub>s</sub> = normalize(Σ<sub>i</sub> a⁰<sub>is</sub> n̂<sub>i</sub>) (M×3 each)"]:::fixed

    REF["e. refinement λ′<sub>is</sub> = λ<sub>is</sub> + w<sub>g</sub>·ξ<sub>is</sub> + b<sub>g</sub>"]:::learned
    PI["e. read-back weights π<sub>is</sub> =<br/>softmax over slices of λ′<sub>is</sub>"]:::fixed
    A1["f. routing a<sub>is</sub> =<br/>softmax over tokens of λ′<sub>is</sub> + ℓ<sub>i</sub>"]:::fixed
    Z["g. slice states Z<sub>s</sub> = Σ<sub>i</sub> a<sub>is</sub> LN(h<sub>i</sub>);<br/>Z<sub>s</sub> += MLP(LN(Z<sub>s</sub>)) (M×D)"]:::learned
    POOL["h. pooled invariants ξ̄<sub>i</sub> = Σ<sub>s</sub> π<sub>is</sub> ξ<sub>is</sub> (N×(5+K));<br/>γ<sub>i</sub> = W<sub>f</sub> ξ̄<sub>i</sub> + b<sub>f</sub> (N×D/2)"]:::learned
    BACK["h. read-back b<sub>i</sub> = Σ<sub>s</sub> π<sub>is</sub> Z<sub>s</sub> (N×D)"]:::fixed
    BR["i. h<sub>i</sub> += W<sub>b</sub> [LN(h<sub>i</sub>); b<sub>i</sub>; γ<sub>i</sub>]"]:::learned
    MLP["j. h<sub>i</sub> += MLP(LN(h<sub>i</sub>))"]:::learned
    OUT["updated token state h<sub>i</sub> (N×D)"]:::data

    H --> L1 --> A0 --> ANC --> XI --> REF
    REF --> PI
    REF --> A1 --> Z --> BACK
    PI --> BACK
    PI --> POOL
    XI --> POOL
    BACK --> BR
    POOL --> BR
    BR --> MLP --> OUT
```

**a. Routing logits.** The layer normalizes the token state and scores it
against one prototype $p_s$ per slice by a cosine at a fixed temperature
$\tau$ (`ROUTING_TEMPERATURE`), so every logit lies in $[-\tau, \tau]$
(`_RoutingLogits`):

$$
\tilde h_i \equiv \mathrm{LN}(h_i), \qquad
\lambda_{is} = \tau\, \frac{\tilde h_i \cdot p_s}{\lVert \tilde h_i \rVert\, \lVert p_s \rVert} .
$$

The prototypes are synthesized per sample from learned base prototypes
$P_s$ (the rows of an $M{\times}D$ matrix) and the sample's own normalized
token states. Each base prototype attends over the tokens with a measure-weighted softmax;
the attended value is centered across the slices and passed through a
smooth bound before it is added to the base prototype:

$$
\Delta_s = \sum_i \operatorname*{softmax}_i\!\left(\tfrac{P_s \cdot W_k \tilde h_i}{\sqrt{D}} + \ell_i\right) W_v \tilde h_i,
\qquad
\tilde\Delta_s = \Delta_s - \tfrac{1}{M}\textstyle\sum_{t} \Delta_{t},
\qquad
p_s = P_s + \frac{\kappa\,\mathrm{rms}(P)}{\mathrm{rms}(\tilde\Delta) + \kappa\,\mathrm{rms}(P)}\, \tilde\Delta_s ,
$$

with $W_k, W_v$ learned $D{\times}D$ maps, $\kappa$ one learned scalar per
block (`gain`) and $\mathrm{rms}$ the root-mean-square entry of a matrix.
Centering removes the component common to every prototype, which carries no
routing information under a cosine. The bound holds the sample-dependent
part to an RMS of at most $\kappa$ times the base prototypes' spread, and a
token cloud whose attention is the same for every base prototype leaves the
prototypes equal to the base prototypes. Token states are invariant, so the prototypes are invariant.

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-routing-constants
#| output: asis
import physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.blocks as _blocks
print(f"In the class, $\\tau = {_blocks.ROUTING_TEMPERATURE:g}$ and $\\kappa$ starts at "
      f"{REF.blocks[0].assign.gain.item():.1f} (`ROUTING_TEMPERATURE`, `_RoutingLogits.gain`); the prototypes "
      f"cost $2D^2 + 1$ parameters per block beyond the base prototypes. What the bound on the logit prevents is in "
      f"@sec-isla-slices.")
```

**b. Provisional routing.** A softmax over the *tokens*, for each slice,
with the measure bias:

$$
a^0_{is} = \frac{\exp(\lambda_{is} + \ell_i)}{\sum_j \exp(\lambda_{js} + \ell_j)} .
$$

Each slice's weights sum to one over the tokens. Any sum $\sum_i a^0_{is}
f_i$ is therefore a measure-weighted mean of $f$ over the slice: a
quadrature estimate of a surface integral (`_softmax_over_points`).

**c. Anchors.** From those weights each slice forms its mean position and
its mean normal direction (`z_pos`, `m_s`):

$$
z_s \equiv \sum_i a^0_{is}\, r_i, \qquad
m_s \equiv \frac{\sum_i a^0_{is}\, \hat n_i}{\big\lvert \sum_i a^0_{is}\, \hat n_i \big\rvert} .
$$

Both are weighted sums of vectors that rotate with the body, with weights
that do not, so the anchors rotate and translate with the body
(@sec-isla-slices).

**d. Relational invariants.** For every token–anchor pair, with the
separation $\rho_{is} \equiv r_i - z_s$ and its direction
$\hat\rho_{is}$, the layer forms $5 + K$ scalars (`_relational_invariants`;
@sec-isla-relational draws them):

$$
\xi_{is} \equiv \big[\,
\lvert\rho_{is}\rvert,\ \log\lvert\rho_{is}\rvert,\
\hat\rho_{is}\!\cdot\!\hat g_1,\ \dots,\ \hat\rho_{is}\!\cdot\!\hat g_K,\
\hat\rho_{is}\!\cdot\!\hat n_i,\
\hat\rho_{is}\!\cdot\! m_s,\
\hat n_i\!\cdot\! m_s
\,\big] .
$$

Every entry is a norm or a dot product of vectors that move together, and
every position appears as a difference, so no origin and no axis is
referred to. A model whose conditions carry vectors or tensors appends, in
the same place, $\hat\rho_{is} \cdot V_{ia}$ for every shared vector
channel and $\hat\rho_{is}^{\mathsf T} T_{ia} \hat\rho_{is}$ for every shared
tensor channel (stage 2). The width is then $5 + K + n_v + n_t$; on the
DrivAerML and AirfRANS tasks it is $5 + K = 6$.

**e. Refinement, and the read-back weights.** A linear map of the
invariants to one scalar per pair refines the routing logit (`geo_logit`),
so a slice can prefer tokens near its anchor, along a global direction from
it, or facing it. The *same* refined logits, normalized over the slices for
each token and without the measure bias, are the read-back weights
(`point_mix`):

$$
\lambda'_{is} = \lambda_{is} + w_g \cdot \xi_{is} + b_g, \qquad
\pi_{is} = \frac{\exp(\lambda'_{is})}{\sum_t \exp(\lambda'_{it})} .
$$

**f. Routing.** The routing weights are recomputed from the refined logits
with the measure bias, exactly as in step b:

$$
a_{is} = \frac{\exp(\lambda'_{is} + \ell_i)}{\sum_j \exp(\lambda'_{js} + \ell_j)} .
$$

@fig-isla-routing-readback shows the two normalizations side by side on
the airfoil: one matrix of logits, read one way as "what each slice
averages" and the other way as "where each token reads from".

**g. Slice states.** Each slice takes the measure-weighted mean of the
normalized token states it routes and transforms it with its own pre-LN
residual MLP (`slice_mlp`):

$$
Z_s = \sum_i a_{is}\, \tilde h_i, \qquad
Z_s \leftarrow Z_s + \mathrm{MLP}_{\mathrm{slice}}(\mathrm{LN}(Z_s)) .
$$

In the surface task this is the only place where tokens exchange
information: through the $M$ slice states, never pairwise.

**h. Read-back.** Each token reads the slice states with its read-back
weights, and reads the invariants pooled with the same weights, projected
to half the width (`back`, `pooled`, `geo_feat`):

$$
b_i = \sum_s \pi_{is}\, Z_s, \qquad
\bar\xi_i = \sum_s \pi_{is}\, \xi_{is}, \qquad
\gamma_i = W_f\, \bar\xi_i + b_f .
$$

The projection is affine and $\pi_{is}$ sums to one over $s$, so pooling
first and projecting second equals projecting every pair and pooling:
$\sum_s \pi_{is}(W_f \xi_{is} + b_f) = W_f \bar\xi_i + b_f$. The order is
a memory decision, not a modeling one (@sec-arch-cost); the identity holds
to $10^{-12}$ in float64 (`test_geo_pool_then_project_is_exact`).

**i. Broadcast.** The normalized token state, what it read, and where it
sits are combined by one affine map into a residual update (`broadcast`):

$$
h_i \leftarrow h_i + W_b\, [\, \tilde h_i;\ b_i;\ \gamma_i \,] .
$$

Steps a to i read the token state only through $\tilde h_i$. This is the
normalized slice reads of @sec-isla-layer: the raw $h_i$ enters the
layer only through the residual identity here and the LayerNorm of step j,
so no block multiplies the stream by a learned matrix.

**j. Token MLP.** A pre-LN residual MLP closes the layer (`norm_mlp`,
`mlp`):

$$
h_i \leftarrow h_i + \mathrm{MLP}(\mathrm{LN}(h_i)) .
$$

```{python}
#| label: fig-isla-routing-readback
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The two softmaxes of a slice layer, on the airfoil with six slices and
#|   eighty cells (hand-made logits that prefer a stretch of arclength stand
#|   in for the learned ones; cells are finer around the leading edge). Top:
#|   the routing weights $a_{is}$, a softmax over tokens for each slice with
#|   the measure bias, so each row sums to one and a slice is a quadrature
#|   average of the cells it covers; the fine leading-edge cells receive
#|   individually smaller weights because they stand for less surface.
#|   Bottom: the read-back weights $\pi_{is}$, a softmax over slices for each
#|   token without the bias, so each column sums to one and a token chooses
#|   where to read. How to read this: both matrices come from the same
#|   logits; the reference configuration has 512 slices per layer and
#|   200,000 tokens per case, so its matrices are far sparser than these. It
#|   does not show a trained model.
#| code-fold: true
frac = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(1.0 - 0.6 * np.sin(np.linspace(0, np.pi, 80)) ** 4)]); frac /= frac[-1]
JJ = joukowski(n_cells=80, frac=frac)      # finer cells around the leading edge (mid-arclength)
s_arc = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(JJ["w"])]); s_mid = (s_arc[:-1] + s_arc[1:]) / 2; total = s_arc[-1]
n_sl = 6
centers = (np.arange(n_sl) + 0.5) / n_sl * total
dd = np.abs(s_mid[:, None] - centers[None, :]); dd = np.minimum(dd, total - dd)
logits = -(dd / (0.06 * total)) ** 2                       # (tokens, slices)
lw_ = np.log(JJ["w"])[:, None]
a = np.exp(logits + lw_); a /= a.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)    # softmax over tokens, per slice
pi = np.exp(logits); pi /= pi.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)        # softmax over slices, per token
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 4.6), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.35))
for ax, mat, title, vmax in ((axes[0], a.T, r"routing $a_{is}$: softmax over tokens, with the measure bias $\ell_i$; each row sums to 1", None),
                             (axes[1], pi.T, r"read-back $\pi_{is}$: softmax over slices, no bias; each column sums to 1", 1.0)):
    im = ax.imshow(mat, aspect="auto", cmap=SEQUENTIAL, vmin=0, vmax=vmax if vmax else mat.max(), interpolation="nearest")
    ax.grid(False); ax.set_yticks(range(n_sl)); ax.set_yticklabels([f"slice {k + 1}" for k in range(n_sl)], fontsize=8.5)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9.5, loc="left", color=INK)
    for sp in ax.spines.values(): sp.set_visible(False)
    cb = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.01); cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=8); cb.outline.set_visible(False)
    cb.set_label("weight [–]", fontsize=8.5)
i_le = int(np.argmin(JJ["mid"][:, 0]))
axes[1].set_xlabel("token $i$ along the surface, from the trailing edge around the leading edge and back [–]", fontsize=9)
for ax in axes:
    ax.axvline(i_le, color=WHITE, lw=1.0, ls="--")
axes[1].text(i_le - 0.8, n_sl - 2, "leading edge", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=8.5, color=WHITE)
plt.show()
```

One slice block's forward is steps a to j in order; `_RoutingLogits` is step a with the prototype synthesis, and `_relational_invariants` is step d on the eager path (the fused kernel of @sec-arch-cost computes the same scalars without storing them).

## Stage 4: the head frame {#sec-arch-head-frame}

**The vector head needs one direction per token that points from the body
to the token, and ISLA takes it from the token's own soft anchor, not from
a center.** After the last layer, one more routing map (`frame_assign`, the
same `_RoutingLogits` form, acting on the final state $h_i$) gives logits
$\lambda^f_{is}$. Read over tokens they give anchors; read over slices they
give each token's soft assignment $\pi^f_{is}$:

$$
a^f_{is} = \frac{\exp(\lambda^f_{is} + \ell_i)}{\sum_j \exp(\lambda^f_{js} + \ell_j)}, \qquad
z^f_s = \sum_i a^f_{is}\, r_i, \qquad
\pi^f_{is} = \frac{\exp(\lambda^f_{is})}{\sum_t \exp(\lambda^f_{it})}, \qquad
u_i = r_i - \sum_s \pi^f_{is}\, z^f_s, \qquad
\hat u_i = u_i / \lvert u_i \rvert .
$$

$u_i$ is a difference of positions, so $\hat u_i$ rotates with the body and
is unchanged by a translation (`a_f`, `z_f`, `b_f`, `r_hat`; @sec-isla-heads
draws the construction). A model whose outputs are all scalars has no head
frame and no `frame_assign` parameters (`needs_frame`).

The head frame reads the raw final state $h_i$, not $\tilde h_i$, so its
logits grow with the residual stream, and on DeepJEB++ its routing
concentrates on so few tokens that the frame degenerates (@sec-deepjeb
measures it). Reading the normalized state there is a candidate fix for that
logit growth that was tested and not adopted: in its registered test, on
AeroZoo's held-out non-box family, it made the pressure error worse on both
seeds, on a field where neither arm beats predicting zero.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Stage 4 in the code"}
The head frame is the tail of `_forward_tokens`: one more routing map, read both ways, and a difference of positions.


## Stage 5: the head {#sec-arch-head}

**One linear head produces every output's invariant coefficients, and each
output of declared rank $r$ is contracted from them over tensor products of
$r$ vectors the token already has.** On the normalized final state
(`norm_out`, `head`):

$$
c_i = W_h\, \mathrm{LN}(h_i) + b_h, \qquad c_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c},
$$

with $n_c$ the sum over the declared outputs of their coefficient counts.
The true basis at token $i$, in the order the code stacks it, is

$$
t_i = \big\{\, \hat g_1, \dots, \hat g_K,\ \hat n_i,\ \hat u_i,\
e_\theta(\hat u_i, \hat n_i),\ e_\theta(\hat u_i, \hat g_1),\ \dots,\ e_\theta(\hat u_i, \hat g_K) \,\big\}
\quad (m = 2K + 3 \text{ vectors}),
$$

with the tangential complement of $\hat u$ against a second direction
$\hat a$ defined, unnormalized, as

$$
e_\theta(\hat u, \hat a) \equiv -\hat a + (\hat a \cdot \hat u)\, \hat u
$$

(`_polar_complement`). It vanishes smoothly where $\hat u \parallel \hat a$,
which is why it is left unnormalized. The pseudovectors are the
Levi-Civita construction from the primaries $\{\hat g_k, \hat n_i, \hat
u_i\}$: their pairwise cross products in three dimensions ($p =
\binom{K+2}{2}$), their perpendiculars in two ($p = K + 2$)
(`_pseudovectors`). An output declared with rank $r$ and even parity is

$$
Y_i = \sum_{j_1 \dots j_r} c_{i\, j_1 \dots j_r}\; t_{i j_1} \otimes \dots \otimes t_{i j_r}
\;+\; \sum_k c_{ik}^{\mathrm{iso}}\, I_k ,
$$

where the isotropic tensors $I_k$ are the identity at rank 2 and the three
products of Kronecker deltas at rank 4 (their symmetric sum for a symmetric
spec). A symmetric spec carries one coefficient per unordered multi-index.
An odd-parity spec replaces exactly one factor by a pseudovector, with the
Levi-Civita symbol as the isotropic term at rank 3. The code gathers the
free coefficients into the full coefficient tensor over ordered
multi-indices and contracts one index at a time, so the $m^r$ products are
never materialized (`_OutputLayout`, `_assemble_output`). @tbl-arch-coeffs
counts the coefficients from the class; ranks above 4 are refused.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-coeffs
#| output: asis
specs = [("scalar (pressure)", {"rank": 0}), ("vector (wall shear stress)", {"rank": 1}),
         ("pseudovector (vorticity)", {"rank": 1, "parity": "odd"}),
         ("rank-2 tensor", {"rank": 2}), ("symmetric rank-2 tensor (stress)", {"rank": 2, "symmetric": True}),
         ("symmetric rank-3 tensor", {"rank": 3, "symmetric": True}), ("symmetric rank-4 tensor", {"rank": 4, "symmetric": True})]
rows = []
for K in (0, 1, 2):
    gs = {f"g{k}": {"rank": 1} for k in range(K)}
    m3 = ISLA(output_schema={f"o{j}": s for j, (_, s) in enumerate(specs)}, boundary_schemas={"vehicle": {}}, global_schema=gs or None, hidden=8, n_layers=1, n_slices=2)
    rows.append([m3.output_layouts[f"o{j}"].n_coeffs for j in range(len(specs))])
out = "| output | $K = 0$ | $K = 1$ | $K = 2$ |\n|---|--:|--:|--:|\n"
for j, (name, _) in enumerate(specs):
    out += f"| {name} | {rows[0][j]} | {rows[1][j]} | {rows[2][j]} |\n"
print(out)
print(": Head coefficients per output field in three dimensions, by the number $K$ of global directions, read from the "
      "class's output layouts (`ISLA.output_layouts[name].n_coeffs`) as the page renders. How to read this: the true basis has "
      "$m = 2K + 3$ vectors, so the vector column is $m$; a field's cost in the head is one row of its width, and the head "
      "is one linear map whatever the outputs are.")
```

The model returns one point-cloud `Mesh`. On an interior task its `points`
are the prediction points. On a surface task they are the given conditions'
cell centroids, the conditions in sorted order and each condition's cells in
its mesh's order, so a per-condition view is a split of the output by the
conditions' cell counts. Its `point_data` holds one leaf per declared output
name, at its natural shape: $(N,)$ at rank 0, $(N, 3)$ at rank 1, $(N, 3,
3)$ at rank 2, and its `global_data` is the selected global inputs, passed
through. Under an
orthogonal map $R$ every true basis vector maps as $R t$, every pseudovector
as $\det(R)\, R t$, and every coefficient is unchanged. An even output
therefore maps as $R^{\otimes r} Y$ and an odd one as $\det(R)\, R^{\otimes
r} Y$. That is the covariance proof, for rotations and reflections alike;
@sec-isla-contracts lists the tests that check it.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Stage 5 in the code"}
The basis is stacked in the order the text gives, and each declared output is contracted from its coefficients one index at a time.

**Almost all of ISLA's parameters are ordinary MLPs; the geometry costs

```{python}
#| label: tbl-isla-params
#| output: asis
def rows_for(m):
    blk = m.blocks[0]; nl = len(m.blocks)
    return [
        ("condition input layer and shared layer (stage 2)", "`boundary_conditions`, `embed`", cnt(m.boundary_conditions) + cnt(m.embed), 1),
        ("routing map, with its LayerNorm (step a)", "`norm_assign`, `assign`", cnt(blk.norm_assign) + cnt(blk.assign), nl),
        ("routing refinement (step e)", "`geo_logit`", cnt(blk.geo_logit), nl),
        ("pooled-invariant projection (step h)", "`geo_feat`", cnt(blk.geo_feat), nl),
        ("slice MLP, with its LayerNorm (step g)", "`slice_mlp`", cnt(blk.slice_mlp), nl),
        ("broadcast (step i)", "`broadcast`", cnt(blk.broadcast), nl),
        ("token MLP, with its LayerNorm (step j)", "`norm_mlp`, `mlp`", cnt(blk.norm_mlp) + cnt(blk.mlp), nl),
        ("head-frame routing map (stage 4)", "`frame_assign`", cnt(m.frame_assign), 1),
        ("head, with its LayerNorm (stage 5)", "`norm_out`, `head`", cnt(m.norm_out) + cnt(m.head), 1),
    ]
R_ = rows_for(REF); TOT = cnt(REF)

for name, code, c, n in R_:
    share = 100 * c * n / TOT
    out += f"| {name} | {code} | {n} | {c:,} | {c * n:,} | {'<0.1' if share < 0.05 else f'{share:.1f}'}% |\n"
out += f"| **total** | | | | **{TOT:,}** | 100% |\n"
out += (f"\n: Parameter count of ISLA in the reference configuration (width {REF.blocks[0].norm_mlp.normalized_shape[0]}, "
        f"{len(REF.blocks)} layers, {REF.n_slices} slices) for the DrivAerML Surface task (a scalar and a vector output, "
        "one global direction), computed from the class as the page renders. How to read this: the two per-layer MLPs and "
        "the broadcast are quadratic in the width and hold most of the total; the routing refinement is the seven numbers of "
        "the geometry (six weights and a bias); the interior task's extra parameters are counted in the text below.\n")
print(out)
```

## The two tasks: surface and interior {#sec-arch-modes}

**The surface task and the interior task share the five stages. They
differ in which points are tokens and which the head reads, and the choice
is made at construction (`interior=False` or `True`).** @fig-isla-modes
places them side by side. Everything above described the first. In the
second, the model draws its boundary tokens from the full-resolution cells
(@sec-arch-boundary-draw), and the prediction points join them before
stage 3. They come in two kinds: *interacting* prediction points (ISLA, the
class default) carry routing mass and write into the slices; *read-only*
prediction points (ISLA-DTT, `query_independent=True`) carry none and read
the boundary cells directly instead (@sec-arch-passive-decoder). The tasks
own different parameter sets (the interior task adds the prediction points'
input layer and, for interacting points, the routing mass), which is why the
task is a constructor argument: a parameter that takes no part in a forward
pass stops distributed training.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-isla-modes
%%| fig-cap: >
%%|   The two tasks of ISLA. Surface (`interior=False`, the default): every boundary cell is a token and
%%|   the head reads every one of them. Interior (`interior=True`): the model draws its boundary tokens from the
%%|   full-resolution cells, and the prediction points join the slice layers as tokens, each with its signed
%%|   distance to the full-resolution surface and its direction computed inside the model, and the head reads them
%%|   alone; interacting points (ISLA) carry a learned routing mass, read-only points (ISLA-DTT) carry none and read
%%|   the boundary cells after every layer.
%%|   How to read this: the slice layer, head frame and head are the same
%%|   modules in every form; only the token set, the prediction points'
%%|   routing mass and the boundary read change. The prediction points' geometry is computed against every cell,
%%|   not against the drawn tokens.
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 460}}}%%
flowchart LR
    classDef data fill:#f4f3ee,stroke:#898781,color:#0b0b0b
    classDef learned fill:#e6f0fb,stroke:#2a78d6,color:#0b0b0b
    classDef fixed fill:#ffffff,stroke:#2a78d6,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#0b0b0b
    classDef aqua fill:#e3f6ef,stroke:#1baf7a,color:#0b0b0b

    subgraph S["surface task"]
        direction TB
        S1["every boundary cell a token (N)"]:::data
        S2["slice layers × 12"]:::learned
        S3["head frame + head on all N tokens"]:::learned
        S1 --> S2 --> S3
    end
    subgraph Q["interior task"]
        direction TB
        Q1["named boundary meshes at full resolution"]:::data
        QD["in-model draw: N boundary tokens<br/>with Horvitz–Thompson measures"]:::fixed
        Q0["exact geometry of each prediction point<br/>against the full-resolution surface"]:::fixed
        Q2["prediction-point tokens (Q): own input layer qt.seed;<br/>routing mass (ISLA) or none (ISLA-DTT)"]:::aqua
        Q3["slice layers × 12 on all N + Q tokens<br/>(ISLA-DTT: + boundary read after each layer)"]:::learned
        Q4["head frame + head on the Q prediction-point tokens"]:::learned
        Q1 --> Q0 --> Q2
        Q1 --> QD --> Q3
        Q2 --> Q3 --> Q4
    end
```

**Prediction points as tokens.** Each prediction point $q$ arrives as a
position $x_q$ alone: the `points` of a point-cloud `Mesh`, whose
`point_data` is not read, or a bare $Q{\times}3$ tensor. A prediction point
has no normal, no area and no condition. The model gives it a direction
$\hat\nu_q$, which plays the normal's part in every invariant, and a signed
distance $s_q$ in length units, both computed from the boundary surface
(@sec-arch-interior-geometry). The point is placed in the same frame, $r_q
= x_q / L$, and has its own input layer (`qt.seed`, a linear map with a
bias, which takes the part a condition's offset takes), followed by the same
shared GELU and linear layer as the boundary tokens (`_QueryTokens`):

$$
h_q \equiv W_e\, \mathrm{GELU}\big(W_{\mathrm q}\, \phi_q + b_{\mathrm q}\big) + b_e ,
\qquad
\phi_q \equiv \big[\, \hat\nu_q \!\cdot\! \hat g_1,\ \dots,\ \hat\nu_q \!\cdot\! \hat g_K,\ \sigma,\
s_q,\ \operatorname{asinh}(s_q / \varepsilon) \,\big] .
$$

The two distance channels are the built-in pair of
@sec-arch-interior-geometry: $s_q$ itself, and its soft logarithm, which
resolves the boundary layer, where $s_q$ is tiny. The prediction points
carry zeros in the shared vector and tensor channels of stage 2.

**Interacting prediction points: routing mass.** In ISLA the prediction
points take part in every softmax over tokens. Their measure bias is not an
area but a learned share of the boundary's total measure, split equally
over the $Q$ points (`qt.logw`, initialized at zero, so the points start
with as much total routing mass as the boundary):

$$
\ell_q = \omega + \log \sum_{i \le N} w_i - \log Q .
$$

Re-representing the same surface on finer cells therefore changes nothing
(`test_query_mass_refinement_invariance`), and rescaling the geometry
shifts every token's bias by the same amount. The $N + Q$ tokens run through
the twelve slice layers together, so the prediction points help form the
prototypes, the anchors and the slice states. The head frame builds its
anchors from all $N + Q$ tokens, and the head reads the $Q$ prediction-point
tokens only. The arrangement is exactly covariant, and the prediction at
one point depends on the other points of the request (@sec-isla-contracts;
measured in @sec-interior-companion).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The interior task in the code"}
The prediction points' tokens are built and appended before the slice layers run; ISLA-DTT's passive measure bias and boundary read are the two branches on `query_independent`.

### The prediction points' geometry {#sec-arch-interior-geometry}

**A prediction point's signed distance and direction come from the exact
closest point on the full-resolution boundary surface, so they are the same
for every draw of the boundary tokens, and they are continuous through the
surface.** Stage 3 needs a direction at every token, and the input layer
above needs a distance to the wall. Both are computed inside the model and
never taken as inputs; the model reads no stored signed-distance field.
Picture a point a hair off an airfoil whose tokens kept every fifth panel:
the nearest kept token is up to a few panels away, but the nearest point of
the airfoil is directly below the point. The model therefore searches the
surface itself, the union of the cells of every given boundary mesh at full
resolution, for the closest point $p_q$ to $x_q$: point to face, never point
to centroid (`exact_boundary_geometry`).

The distance is signed by the pseudo-normal $\hat N_q$ of the feature $p_q$
lies on: the cell's normal inside a cell; on an edge or a vertex the sum of
the normals of the cells that share it, angle-weighted at a vertex in three
dimensions (the construction of Bærentzen and Aanæs). The pseudo-normal
gets the sign right behind a sharp trailing edge and at a concave corner,
where the normal of the one closest cell would flip it. The distance is
positive on the side the cells' normals point to; the recipe orients each
dataset's boundary with a transform set per dataset file
(`FlipBoundaryOrientation`). The direction $u_q$ points from the surface to
the point: the closest cell's normal turned toward the point when $p_q$ is
inside a cell, the unit difference otherwise. The token then reads the
distance in length units and the direction times the sign of the distance,
which is the gradient of the signed distance. @fig-arch-exact-geometry
draws both on the airfoil, with the class's own functions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-arch-exact-geometry
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The prediction points' geometry on the airfoil of @fig-arch-boundary-draw, computed by the class's
#|   `exact_boundary_geometry` and `soft_log_length` as the page renders. Top, mid-chord on both surfaces: prediction
#|   points (aqua) joined by solid lines to their exact closest points $p_q$ on the full 160-cell polyline (gray), and
#|   by dotted lines to the nearest token of two training-mode draws of 32 tokens (open and filled dots); the solid
#|   lines are the model's geometry, the dotted ones show what a nearest-token search would read instead. Bottom: the
#|   two distance channels, $s$ (aqua) and $\operatorname{asinh}(s / \varepsilon)$ (blue), against the signed
#|   distance $s$ in length units, on an axis that is linear within $\pm\varepsilon = \pm 10^{-6}$ (the gray band, where
#|   the soft logarithm is linear) and logarithmic outside. How to read this: the exact geometry does not depend on which tokens were
#|   drawn, and the soft logarithm passes through zero with a finite slope, so a point on the wall reads what its
#|   neighbors on either side read. It does not show a trained model.
#| fig-height: 6.0
#| code-fold: true
from physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.geometry import exact_boundary_geometry, soft_log_length, LENGTH_SOFTENING
xy_g = torch.tensor(JD["xy"][:-1], dtype=torch.float64)
n_g = len(xy_g)
cells_g = torch.stack([(torch.arange(n_g) + 1) % n_g, torch.arange(n_g)], -1)   # oriented so the normals point out of the body
x0, x1 = -0.2, 0.9                                                                # the window: mid-chord, both surfaces
pick = [i for i in range(n_g) if x0 + 0.1 < JD["mid"][i, 0] < x1 - 0.1][::5]
qs = np.concatenate([JD["mid"][pick] + off * JD["nrm"][pick] for off in (0.035, 0.09)])
d_g, u_g = exact_boundary_geometry(torch.tensor(qs), xy_g, cells_g)
p_g = qs - (d_g[:, None] * torch.where((d_g >= 0)[:, None], u_g, -u_g)).numpy()
draws = [sample_boundary_cells([a_d], [x_d], BUDGET_D, torch.tensor(u0, dtype=torch.float64))[0].numpy() for u0 in (0.13, 0.71)]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8.0, 6.0), gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1.3, 1.0], hspace=0.3))
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(JD["xy"][:, 0], JD["xy"][:, 1], color=MUTED, lw=1.4)
for k, (kd, mfc) in enumerate(zip(draws, (WHITE, INK))):
    tok = JD["mid"][kd]
    for q in qs:
        j = int(np.argmin(((tok - q) ** 2).sum(1)))
        ax.plot([q[0], tok[j, 0]], [q[1], tok[j, 1]], ls=":", lw=0.9, color=INK if k else MUTED)
    ax.plot(tok[:, 0], tok[:, 1], "o", ms=5, mfc=mfc, mec=INK, mew=0.8, zorder=4)
for q, p in zip(qs, p_g):
    ax.plot([q[0], p[0]], [q[1], p[1]], color=AQUA, lw=1.8)
ax.plot(qs[:, 0], qs[:, 1], "o", color=AQUA, ms=5, zorder=5)
ax.set_xlim(x0, x1); ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off")
ax = axes[1]
s_ax = np.concatenate([-np.logspace(0, -9, 400), [0.0], np.logspace(-9, 0, 400)])
y_ax = soft_log_length(torch.tensor(s_ax)).numpy()
ax.axvspan(-LENGTH_SOFTENING, LENGTH_SOFTENING, color="#ecebe6", lw=0)
ax.plot(s_ax, y_ax, color=BLUE, lw=1.8)
ax.plot(s_ax, s_ax, color=AQUA, lw=1.4)
label_line(ax, 1e-2, float(soft_log_length(torch.tensor(1e-2))), r"$\mathrm{asinh}(s/\varepsilon)$", BLUE, dy=-3.0)
label_line(ax, 1e-2, 1e-2, r"$s$", AQUA, dy=2.0)
ax.set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=LENGTH_SOFTENING)
ax.set_xticks([-1, -1e-3, -1e-6, 0, 1e-6, 1e-3, 1]); ax.set_xticklabels(["−1", "−0.001", "−10⁻⁶", "0", "10⁻⁶", "0.001", "1"])
ax.set_xlabel("signed distance in length units $s = \\delta / L$ [–]"); ax.set_ylabel("channel value [–]")
for sp in ("top", "right"): ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

In symbols, with $\hat n_f$ the normal of the cell $f$ that holds $p_q$:

$$
\delta_q \equiv \operatorname{sign}\big((x_q - p_q) \cdot \hat N_q\big)\, \lvert x_q - p_q \rvert,
\qquad
u_q \equiv \begin{cases}
  \operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\, \hat n_f & p_q \text{ inside the cell } f, \\
  (x_q - p_q) / \lvert x_q - p_q \rvert & \text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
$$

$$
s_q \equiv \delta_q / L, \qquad
\big[\, s_q,\ \operatorname{asinh}(s_q / \varepsilon) \,\big], \qquad
\hat\nu_q \equiv \operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\, u_q, \quad \operatorname{sign}(0) \equiv +1 .
$$

A point on the surface ($\lvert x_q - p_q \rvert$ at most `EPS`) takes
$\delta_q = 0$ and $u_q = \hat N_q$; coincident vertices are welded first, so
a surface stored in pieces, one mesh per condition, has the pseudo-normals
of the surface it describes. Inside a cell $\hat\nu_q = \hat n_f$ on both
sides of the wall, and $\operatorname{asinh}(s / \varepsilon)$ is $s /
\varepsilon$ near zero and $\operatorname{sign}(s) \log(2 \lvert s \rvert /
\varepsilon)$ far from it (`soft_log_length`): the code of a point is
continuous through the surface, so a point on it, whose distance is zero or
a rounding error of either sign, reads what the points just off it read on
either side. The softening $\varepsilon$ is a numerical resolution in the
length unit, not a parameter: above float32's resolution of a distance
relative to $L$ and below the finest wall spacing of the reference datasets
(the docstring of `soft_log_length` gives both).

$\delta_q$ and $u_q$ are functions of the surface and its orientation alone:
the same for every draw of the boundary tokens, unchanged by splitting a
cell, and converging as $O(h^2)$ under refinement of a smooth surface, like
a stored signed-distance field computed from the same surface. Both are
built from a difference of positions, so $\delta_q$ is invariant and $u_q$
covariant under every rigid motion and reflection (with the cells
re-oriented so that their normals follow the map), and $\delta_q$ scales
with the geometry. $s_q = \delta_q / L$ is the same for every draw too,
since $L$ is computed from the full-resolution boundary before the draw
(stage 1).

The search runs in `forward`, where the meshes are, before the draw, at the
points' precision and outside autocast. In three dimensions it is a Warp
bounding-volume-hierarchy query over the triangles (a torch custom
operator, in float32, whose closest cell differs from the exact one only at
a tie at float32 resolution); in two it is an exact brute force over the
segments, chunked over the points (`_closest_cell`). The interior task is
implemented in two and three dimensions. The search runs without gradient;
the closest point is then rebuilt from its cell's vertices with the
barycentric weights of its region of the cell (computed in float64), so
$\delta_q$ and $u_q$ are differentiable in the points and the vertex
positions.

**Two choices in this geometry are made by rounding.** At a point equally
far from two or more features of the surface, such as a node on the
mid-thickness plane of a plate, the search keeps the first closest feature
it meets, so the order of the mesh's vertices picks $u_q$. At a fold of the
surface, where cells meet back to back, the pseudo-normal that signs
$\delta_q$ is a sum of unit normals that cancels exactly, so roundoff picks
the sign, which is ill-posed even in exact arithmetic. Neither has a
convergent knob; @sec-medial-ties measures both, and a tie rule that reads
every feature within float32 resolution of the minimum is an open question
(@sec-oq-ties).

```{python}
#| label: para-arch-sdf-configs
#| output: asis
def _model_block(name):
    cfg = yaml.safe_load((CONF / f"{name}.yaml").read_text())
    blk = dict(cfg.get("model", {}))
    for parent in cfg.get("defaults", []) or []:
        if isinstance(parent, str):
            base = yaml.safe_load((CONF / f"{parent}.yaml").read_text()).get("model", {})
            blk = {**base, **blk}
    return cfg, blk
interior_cfgs = sorted(p.stem for p in CONF.glob("isla_*.yaml") if _model_block(p.stem)[1].get("interior"))
fmt = lambda xs: ", ".join(f"`{x}`" for x in xs)
print(f"The prediction points' only input is their positions. The recipe's interior ISLA configurations are "
      f"{fmt(interior_cfgs)} (read from `conf/model/` as the page renders), and none of them gives ISLA a stored "
      "signed-distance field.")
```

**What the exact geometry measures.** Two pre-registered comparisons
isolate this stage (@tbl-arch-geo-evidence), the first on the AirfRANS
interior task, the second on it and on PLAID Tensile2d and the GINOT lug. The
first replaces the nearest-token geometry of the nearest-token form
(@sec-checkpoint-form) by the exact geometry, read through a signed
logarithm $\operatorname{sign}(s_q) \log(\lvert s_q \rvert + 10^{-12})$;
the second keeps the exact geometry and replaces that channel by
$\operatorname{asinh}(s_q / \varepsilon)$ and the direction $u_q$ by
$\operatorname{sign}(\delta_q)\, u_q$, the encoding above. Every arm
except the first comparison's control reads the exact built-in geometry,
and every arm is otherwise of the nearest-token form: it still reads the
stored signed distance and its direction as a prediction-point input on all
three datasets (the second comparison's variant encodes that channel as it
encodes $s_q$). The class reads no stored field, so neither comparison is a
measurement of the class; they are the registered tests that chose the
design, and @tbl-arch-attrib, below, measures the class. Chapter 4 gives what
the exact geometry does to the contracts (@sec-exact-geometry-draw,
@sec-medial-ties).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-geo-evidence
#| output: asis
GE = json.load(open(RES / "campaigns_2026-10-19" / "geo_evidence" / "geo_evidence.json"))
g1, gc = GE["geo1_airfrans"], GE["geo_cont"]
AFF = (("pressure_l2", "pressure"), ("velocity_l2", "velocity"), ("nut_l2", "eddy viscosity"))
def seeds_of(arm, f):
    return [arm[f]["per_seed"][s] for s in ("42", "43")]
def row(label, var, ctl, f, fname, in_rule):
    v, c = seeds_of(var, f), seeds_of(ctl, f)
    r = np.mean(v) / np.mean(c)
    side = "below" if max(v) < min(c) else ("above" if min(v) > max(c) else "overlap")
    return f"| {label} | {fname} | {np.mean(c):.5f} | {np.mean(v):.5f} | {r:.3f} | {' / '.join(f'{x / y:.3f}' for x, y in zip(v, c))} | {side} | {in_rule} |\n"
out = ("| comparison (variant ÷ control) | field | control | variant | ratio | per seed | variant seeds vs control seeds | in the registered rule |\n"
       "|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|---|\n")
for f, fname in AFF:
    out += row("exact geometry ÷ nearest-token geometry, AirfRANS", g1["geo1"]["native"], g1["a2s"]["native"], f, fname, "–")
dec = []
for ds, lab, fields in (("af", "AirfRANS", AFF), ("t2dz", "PLAID Tensile2d", (("displacement_l2", "displacement"), ("stress_l2", "stress"), ("q_l2", "q"))),
                        ("lug", "GINOT lug", (("von_mises_l2", "von Mises stress"),))):
    for f, fname in fields:
        rule = "yes" if (ds == "af" or f == "displacement_l2") else "no"
        if rule == "yes":
            dec.append(gc[ds]["cont_over_ctl"]["native"][f])
        out += row(f"continuous encoding ÷ signed-log encoding, {lab}", gc[ds]["cont"]["native"], gc[ds]["ctl"]["native"], f, fname, rule)
print(out)
G_dec = float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(dec))))
print(f": The exact-geometry evidence: area-weighted relative L2 of each control and variant, seed means of two seeds (42, 43) "
      f"and the per-seed ratios paired by seed, native meshes, float32, final checkpoints. Instrument: ISLA at the reference "
      f"configuration with the normalized slice reads, both arms of a comparison trained alike, every arm reading the stored "
      f"signed distance as a prediction-point input beside its built-in geometry; AirfRANS uniform interior "
      f"task, 200 test cases; PLAID Tensile2d and the GINOT lug on their interior tasks. Results: "
      f"results/campaigns_2026-10-19/geo_evidence/geo_evidence.json (`geo1_airfrans`, `geo_cont`). How to read this: a "
      f"ratio compares two ISLA variants, the variant over its control, and below one means the variant is more accurate; "
      f"\"below\" means both variant seeds lie below both control seeds. The registered rule of the second comparison read "
      f"its four marked fields: their geometric mean ratio is {G_dec:.3f}, inside its adoption bar (at most 1.01, with no field "
      f"at 1.10 or more); the other fields were reported beside the rule. The first comparison's control is the standing's "
      f"ISLA arm, of the nearest-token form (@sec-checkpoint-form). The table does not compare ISLA with a baseline.")
```
